brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Portwise, the freight visibility platform in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: dependable and calm, for operations teams who look at it all day; serious enough for enterprise procurement. No globes, ships, containers, trucks or arrows. Web app, sales decks and LinkedIn.

claim.notes: Beş yön iki turda elendi (üçü sketch incelemesinde, ikisi kritik kapısında: Drawn Word 5,4 ve Flat Arch 4,2 ortalama), bu yüzden finalize, export ve gallery çalıştırılmadı; ayrıca PORTWISE adı için doğrulanmamış bir marka çakışması riski var.

concepts.title: Flat Arch
readsAs: a plain lowercase w in a squared geometric font (or Greek omega)
the wordmark reads 'partwise' because the flat-sided o looks like a single-storey a
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as (word at 28-32 px, from cmp2): s1 'portwise' in a squared, rounded-rect display grotesk (Eurostile/esports family) - techy, not calm; its p icon alone reads as a parking-sign P, struck. s2 a tall condensed squared sans, like port/rail signage - the calmest and most structural of the three, the slim posts do faintly suggest a colonnade; w icon reads as a plain W, holds at 16 px. s3 heavy blocky squared display - techy/gaming, contradicts calm; S icon generic. Keep s2. Risks: the 'flat arch' idea is not visible yet - it reads as a squared condensed typeface, not arcades; the w built from two inverted u's reads as 'uu'; the r is a stub; the orange square i-dot is a stock accent; at 16 px the word is mush (fine, the icon carries 16 px). Fix: make the arch shoulder the one unmistakable drawn feature (one consistent radius into a flat top, repeated in p/o/r/s/e), widen the x-height slightly toward calm, redraw w as a single shape, keep corners soft not squircle-tech, and cut the icon from that exact arch so it does not read as a bare W.

concepts.title: Berth
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a parking sign (P with a parked car); s2 a P with a slot / Pac-man mouth, still parking; s3 a lowercase 'a' or 'q' with a block in it, a different letter. All struck: the dominant reading is the parking-sign P, and the gold block inside reads as a container, which the brief excludes; it is also the name's initial with an object nested in the counter, the common monogram device. Reworking the bay will not escape 'parking'. Different move: drop the initial-with-object idea; if a letter carries the identity, let the wordmark concept own it, and give berth's 'held in place' idea a non-letter form (e.g. the calm of a mooring line or a quay edge as pure proportion) without boxes.

concepts.title: Quay
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a hamburger/burger bun or bread loaf over a tray (UI burger-adjacent; also 0.65 visual to project44 icon, review risk); s2 a half-dome over a bar - sunset/helmet/mushroom/bell, sunsets already struck; s3 a roof over a slab - barn/house or tank, and a cut-and-shift device; s4 a toaster/mailbox/rounded loaf over a shelf, at 16 px a printer-like UI glyph. None reads as stone meeting water: the horizontal gap reads as a split between two objects, not a waterline, and every sketch is the same 'rounded mass sliced by one bar with an offset' - the generic cut device on a blob. All struck. Different move: drop the slice. Try one unbroken silhouette whose edge carries the idea - e.g. a quay wall in section (a single solid mass with one distinctive stepped or battered face meeting open negative space), or the mark as negative space: water defined by a calm, heavy land contour around it. One contour, no internal gap, asymmetric so it cannot read as a bun, dome or button.

concepts.title: Range
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s5 a horizontal bar chart / left-aligned-text icon (the brief explicitly bans the bar-chart look); s6 a toggle switch or battery, the same toggle reading that struck the first round, and the hollow lower pill reads as a D cut-out; s7 a list/menu icon or a loading-dots progress indicator, muddy at 16 px (86%), and it is still bars. All three struck. The range idea (known vs. forecast) keeps collapsing into horizontal bars and pills because it is drawn as data. Different move: stop drawing a chart. Try one closed, calm, non-rectilinear form whose outline is known on one side and given only as a contour or open edge on the other (one solid half carried on by a line of the same weight to the same boundary), or carry the known/estimate split in the wordmark itself. No rows, no rounded bars, no pills, nothing that can be read as a control.

concepts.title: Drawn Word
readsAs: a plain geometric-sans lowercase wordmark (Gilroy/Futura-like) with a slightly joined r-t
a squared 'P' like a parking sign
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 an info 'i' icon / a lollipop, the error-bar reading only comes after explanation; s2 an 'rt' ligature with a flat shared roof, a little like a lintel or torii; s3 a no-entry sign or theta (82% stock shape) - struck. s1 struck as UI info icon. Pick s2: the only move that lives in the word rather than beside it, calm and structural, fits enterprise-serious. Risks to fix: the r must stay legible as r (it can read as n or a Cyrillic p at 16 px) - keep a visible r terminal or roof overhang left of the stem; set it inside the full 'portwise' word early, because 'rt' alone is not the name and is not an avatar. Decide the standalone icon now (likely the p or 'po' carrying the same flat-roof logic), not as an afterthought. Keep amber out unless it earns a role.
